Would swapping city trucks onto the corridor save fuel?

Short answer: not by swapping — the gap is about duty cycle and idling, not which truck runs where; and the two roles need different weight classes.

  • Highway is already the efficient duty. The heavy corridor trucks run ~9.5–9.9 L/100km with the lowest idling per km (~0.5 h/100km). Moving a heavy truck into city work would raise its consumption.
  • City work is the costly duty. The light Riyadh pickups idle 2–4× more per km (~1.3–2.0 h/100km, 200+ idle hours each) — fuel burned for zero distance.
  • Weight-class mismatch blocks a real swap. The corridor needs the payload of a heavy شاحنة; the city units are light بكب pickups. They are not interchangeable for the same freight.
  • Where the savings are: cut idling on the light pickups (halving ~200 idle h each ≈ 150–300 L saved per truck); keep the heavy corridor trucks fully loaded (and flag any truck showing an implausibly low L/100km — under ~4 — which points to under-reported fills).

Economy = litres filled ÷ GPS distance; idling fuel assumed ~1.5 L/h; no payload data, so the class-fit judgement is operational, not measured.

Anonymized: no plate, company, VIN or IMEI. Base-map tiles load from OpenStreetMap at view time.
